question: In 1979, who shared the Nobel Prize with Georg Wittig for their 'development of the use of boron- and phosphorus-containing compounds, respectively, into important reagents in organic synthesis'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Herbert C Brown**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1979 Nobel Prize for Chemistry** has been awarded jointly to Georg Wittig of the University of Heidelberg and Herbert C. Brown of Purdue University for their separate work in organic synthesis
 
• Wittig's major achievement was the development of a highly specific method for the synthesis of olefins
 
• Brown found major new routes to add substituents to olefins selectively
 
• Both employed elements that had found little previous use in organic synthesis, and both prospered by following up on unexpected observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Noble Prize award was conferred in **1901**.
 
• It is given in the name of **Alfred Noble** who was a Swedish Inventor.
 
• The Nobel Prize is awarded yearly to the individual or organization who do an extraordinary job in the field of **Physics, Chemistry, Literature, Peace, Physiology, and Economics**.
 
• All the Noble Prizes are given in Stockholm, Sweden except for the Noble Peace prize which is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
